focus_area_title: Develop a Habit of Recognizing Input
content_text_body:
Thanking your team members is one of the simplest and most effective ways to communicate that you value hearing their ideas, suggestions, and perspectives. The goal here is to develop a regular practice of meaningfully recognizing your team's input.

For starters, read this brief article to get the big picture: Are You Using Recognition Effectively?  

### For one week, just observe

Jot down all of the times that any team member shared an idea, insight, perspective, or suggestion with you. Review the list at the end of each day.

### Then practice daily

Consistently say "thank youâ€ for all your team members' efforts sharing their feedback and ideas. Close out every conversation or meeting recognizing and thanking them for their input. 

### Create a trigger for yourself

for example:

> In my weekly 1:1 with each team member, I will start by thanking them for their input and suggestions that week and recognize the value it brought to the team.

Thank them. Let them know what they said, why it was important for the team and the business, and how you plan to follow up on an idea or suggestion. 

### Commit to writing just one thank-you per week

Each week, jot down each team member's biggest accomplishment for the week. Then pick one, and send him or her a thank-you note. Let that team member know the impact of what they did, why it was important for the team and the business - and whenever possible - what others are saying about it.  

### Create a feedback loop

Ask your team to give you feedback at the end of each week on how consistently you're demonstrating that you heard and value their input and ideas.
